solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bridge? It could be pontoon

definitions.meaning: bridge is a trick-taking game played with a pack of cards
pontoon, the British name for blackjack, is another example of a game played with cards

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a floating pontoon would serve as a bridge across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the engineering sense: a pontoon bridge floats on boats. Both bridge and pontoon (British blackjack) are also games played with cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a classic partnership game played with a deck of fifty-two cards.

clue.text: Leap from horse-drawn carriage, falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the carriage word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a cabriolet is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by one horse

explanation.surface: Someone takes a leap from a horse-drawn carriage and doesn't quite make it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' drops T from the end of CABRIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriole is a ballet jump in which the legs are beaten together in the air.

clue.text: Give up area of responsibility

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to cancel or refrain from inflicting a debt or punishment
as a noun, the scope of a person's or body's duties

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the part of the job they were in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit a debt is to forgo it, and one's brief or scope of duties is also called this.

clue.text: The woman's relations will first want good bit of food

indicators.note: will first want says the good piece leads before the family words

parts.note: the woman's means her
relations are kin

explanation.surface: A woman's family will expect a decent bite to eat before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will first want' puts G at the front of HER and KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherkin is a small pickled cucumber, a morsel eaten as a relish or snack.

clue.text: Catastrophe coming up brings low spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: doom is catastrophe or ruin

explanation.surface: A disaster approaching leaves people feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses DOOM in this down entry; 'brings' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mood means being in a sulky or gloomy state of mind.

clue.text: Top spot for the traditional writer?

definitions.text: Top spot for the traditional writer?

parts.words: Top spot for the traditional writer?
parts.note: the starving author of legend works in a cramped room right under the roof, the topmost spot in the house

explanation.surface: A question about the best position or place for an old-fashioned author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top spot' sounds like first place or a ranking, but it means the highest room in a building, where the impoverished writer traditionally lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room, the stereotypical lodging of the poor struggling author.

clue.text: What nice gal could be?

indicators.note: could be invites the letters of the phrase to become something else

explanation.surface: Asking what a pleasant girl might be described as.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NICE GAL, and a nice gal could indeed be described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means sweet and good-natured, like an angel, which a nice girl might be.

clue.text: About to join new church, always needing to join in respectful worship

indicators.note: to join in tells the solver to insert the word for always into the other pieces

parts.note: re is Latin for about or concerning
ever means always
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a church and is always required to take part in its devout services.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'to join in' does the inserting; the earlier 'to join' is only a link. RE is the crossword's Latin 'about', CE the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect or veneration, the attitude of worship.

clue.text: Grease rope to keep everything secure

indicators.note: to keep says the rope holds the other word within it
secure completes the idea of the rope keeping something safely wrapped inside it

parts.note: a tow is a rope used for pulling
everything means all

explanation.surface: Lubricate the rope so that everything is tied down securely.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is split: 'to keep' and 'secure' together say the rope holds the other word, with 'everything' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, a hard grease used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Killed, as one may be in a dodgem car!

definitions.meaning: slang for murdered or done away with

definitions.text: as one may be in a dodgem car!
definitions.meaning: in a fairground dodgem you can literally be knocked off course by another car's collision

explanation.surface: Someone at the fairground gets killed, or merely jolted, while driving a dodgem car.
explanation.walkthrough: A dodgem is a small electric bumper car at a fairground; being struck by one can knock you off, which is also slang for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done in, murdered, is gangster slang using the same phrase as being knocked aside.

clue.text: Outrageous tirade beneath the national symbol?

indicators.note: beneath places the tirade below the symbol in this down entry

parts.note: a flag is a nation's symbol
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: Someone launches an outrageous outburst standing below the country's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'beneath' puts RANT under FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means shockingly obvious and offensive, conspicuously outrageous.

clue.text: A lot will go after it's gone down

definitions.text: A lot will go after it's gone down

parts.words: A lot will go after it's gone down
parts.note: at an auction, each lot is sold once the auctioneer's hammer has struck the block

explanation.surface: Plenty of people will leave once something has gone down, perhaps a ship or the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like 'many', but it is an auction lot, which is sold ('will go') once the auctioneer's hammer has come down.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's small hammer is brought down to mark that a lot has been sold.

clue.text: New recruits in army only half eager

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: only half says just the first two of the four letters of the synonym are used

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits join the army but are only half enthusiastic about it.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve. 'only half' keeps KE, the first half of KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intake is the batch of people newly admitted to an organisation, such as recruits.

clue.text: Barrier behind which is a river with two ducks and a wild beast

indicators.note: behind which is places the following pieces after the barrier's letters

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are two O shapes

explanation.surface: Behind a wall lie a river, two ducks and a wild animal, like a farmyard scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds, but a duck in cricket is a score of zero, so two ducks give OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaroo is a large Australian kangaroo species living in the wild.

clue.text: Maiden being dressed in coarse cloth as an abusive punishment?

indicators.note: being dressed in means the maiden is clothed, so placed inside the cloth word

parts.note: sacking is coarse cloth
M is a maiden over in cricket

explanation.surface: Making a maiden wear coarse sackcloth as a cruel penance.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; 'being dressed in' puts it inside SACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacking is striking a child with the hand, a punishment many now consider abuse.

clue.text: A neat criminal working — a Brazilian maybe

indicators.note: working signals that the letters are being put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy crook at work turns out to be someone from Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of A NEAT CRIMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian is one example of a person from the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking Americas, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Experimental spin in cricket match leading to attacking shot?

indicators.note: leading to puts the match word before the shot word

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match
a drive is an attacking stroke in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: A slow bowler's trial spin delivery in a cricket match ends in an aggressive stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' suggests bowling in the cricket surface, but means a drive in a car. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test drive is a trial run in a car, colloquially a spin.

clue.text: Fish starts to swim terrifically with impulse to get on

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: an urge is an impulse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish begins swimming tremendously fast, with an impulse to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives ST from swim and terrifically; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish famed as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Somehow offend clients, being certain of one's own abilities

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: A business somehow insults its customers while being sure of its own skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges the letters of OFFEND CLIENTS; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being assured of your own powers is the meaning of the compound adjective.

clue.text: A GB dog no longer needs this excess freedom

definitions.text: A GB dog no longer needs this
definitions.meaning: British dog owners once needed a permit for their pets, abolished in 1987

explanation.surface: A British dog no longer requires something that gives too much liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog permits were abolished in Great Britain in 1987 (Northern Ireland kept them).
explanation.definitionFit: Licence also means excessive liberty of behaviour, freedom without restraint.

clue.text: Over time I am needing scheme to be put in place

indicators.note: over in a down entry puts the preceding pieces above the time letter

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Over time I need to have a scheme put into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Over' means placed above, so the first pieces sit on top of the time letter; 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to insert or fix something firmly in position.

clue.text: Notice university lecturer's supplementary items

parts.note: an ad is a notice
a don is a university lecturer, and don's gives the letters with the s

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a university lecturer's extra bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge; the possessive supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Add-ons are extras supplied in addition to a main product.

clue.text: Splendid act I completed, partially educational

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer boasts of finishing a splendid act that was partly educational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' points to the run DIDACTIC inside splenDID ACT I Completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic describes something intended to teach or instruct.

clue.text: Astronaut will make Mars finally, given speed, right?

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of the planet's name

parts.note: speed means pace

explanation.surface: Asking whether a space traveller will reach the planet Mars in the end if given enough speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes S, the last letter of Mars; 'will make' and 'given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a science-fiction term for one who travels in outer space.

clue.text: Poetic country that's cold and green

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A verse describing a land that is cold and green, like Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clime is a literary word for a region or its climate.

clue.text: Twelve people endlessly stuck on a Scottish island

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the panel word

parts.note: a jury traditionally has twelve members

explanation.surface: Twelve jurors stranded on a remote Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops Y from JURY; 'stuck on' is a link adding A.
explanation.definitionFit: Jura is an island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Yellow particle that may be seen in the night sky

definitions.text: that may be seen in the night sky

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A small yellow speck that might be spotted in the sky at night.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold or yellow in heraldry, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a prominent constellation visible in the night sky.

clue.text: Chemical in excess supply taken to a pit

parts.note: a glut is an excess supply
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A surplus of some chemical is carted off to a pit for disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'taken to' are links joining the definition and the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutamine is an amino acid, a chemical compound found in proteins.

clue.text: Editor gets stuck into recent information about European country

indicators.note: gets stuck into places the editor inside the other piece
about here means turned round, so the word for news is read backwards

parts.note: news is recent information

explanation.surface: An editor gets absorbed in the latest news concerning a European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for recent information, giving SWEN, and 'gets stuck into' places the editor inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation in northern Europe.

clue.text: One god joining the cricket side that has lots of gods

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
the on side in cricket is the half of the field on the batsman's leg side

explanation.surface: A single deity joins a cricket team that is full of gods, sporting heroes perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side, giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the whole collection of the deities of a people, or a temple to them all.
